speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with gait and limb ataxia; to begin narrowing down the cause of this neurological deficit, have you noticed any recent memory loss, confusion, or personality changes? Additionally, could you describe the specific nature of your gait disturbance and any history of head trauma or substance use?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms suggest cerebellar dysfunction; given your significant medical history, have you ever been diagnosed with Wilson's disease or suffered from chronic alcohol use? Also, are you experiencing any tremors, difficulty swallowing, or speech slurring?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) due to natalizumab therapy.

I will proceed with the final diagnosis based on the confirmed history of Crohn's disease, natalizumab use, and the clinical presentation of cerebellar ataxia, as further questioning is unnecessary for this established etiology.
